title: Microsoft Intune: granular RBAC permissions for endpoint security workloads
notes: claim 53: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the assignment guidance omits the exception for unlicensed administrators in nested groups, and the cited Graph assignment reference does not document setting the administrator groups. The licensing paragraph also omits the unlicensed-administrator exception and promises unchanged EDR licensing without supporting documentation. The roadmap facts and the description of the partly completed permission transition are supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether existing custom or built-in roles gain, keep or lose workload access when the new permissions arrive.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune granular endpoint security RBAC permissions existing custom roles migration automatic default Security baselines Antivirus Firewall Disk encryption. Opened manage-policies, create-custom-role, assign-role and What's new; no migration or inheritance rule found.

claims.claim: Learn documents no released workload-specific alternative to Security baselines for granting Antivirus, Firewall or Disk encryption policy access.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune Firewall Antivirus Disk encryption policies permission Security baselines custom role granular. Read manage-policies and custom-role permissions; searched What's new for granular, RBAC and Antivirus permission. No released alternative found for these endpoint security policy types.

claims.claim: Every member of an assigned Admin Group receives the role's permissions without qualification.
claims.quote: If your tenant allows unlicensed admins, Intune role assignments only apply to direct members of the assigned security group. Members of nested groups do not receive these assignments by default.
claims.fix: Qualify both occurrences: 'Every direct member receives the role's permissions. If the tenant allows unlicensed admins, nested-group members do not receive the assignment by default; a nested-group user with an Intune licence does receive the role.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/role-based-access-control/assign-role.

claims.claim: Intune RBAC permissions govern administrators' management access rather than granting end users administrative roles.
claims.quote: RBAC roles to users who administer your Intune subscription. RBAC roles are assigned to groups, and not individual users.

claims.claim: Defender portal security settings management uses the same Intune RBAC permissions.
claims.quote: Security settings management through the Defender portal uses the same Intune RBAC permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enabled Multi Admin Approval can require a second administrator to approve role permission, admin group or member group assignment changes.
claims.quote: When this setting is on, a second administrator must approve changes to roles. These changes can include updates to role permissions, admin groups, or member group assignments. The change takes effect only after the approval.

claims.claim: Learn names Endpoint Security Manager, Help Desk Operator and Read Only Operator as built-in roles with endpoint security access.
claims.quote: Endpoint Security Manager - Full management capabilities across all endpoint security policies. Help Desk Operator - Limited operational tasks and read access. Read Only Operator - View-only access to policies and reports.

claims.claim: Custom roles can include any Intune RBAC permission.
claims.quote: These custom roles can include any Intune RBAC permission, allowing for refined admin access and support for the principle of least-privileged access within the organization.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/role-based-access-control/overview to sources for the statement that custom roles can include any Intune RBAC permission.

claims.claim: Learn says the Microsoft Entra Intune Service Administrator role is needed to create, edit or assign custom roles.
claims.quote: To create, edit, or assign roles, your account must have the following role in Microsoft Entra ID: Intune Service Administrator
claims.fix: Retain the attribution to the custom-role page, but add: 'The assignment page instead documents Intune Role Administrator as the least-privileged built-in role, or a custom role with Roles Assign/Create/Delete/Read/Update and Organization Read, for managing RBAC roles and assignments.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/role-based-access-control/assign-role. Apply this qualification to the control note and repeated role requirement.

claims.claim: The permissions are a new option within the licensed Intune service, so the licensing model is included.
claims.quote: Microsoft Intune Plan 1: the base service. Cloud-based unified endpoint management for devices and apps. ... An Intune license is required for any user or device that benefits directly or indirectly from the Microsoft Intune service

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Any user or device benefiting from Intune requires an Intune licence, without an administrator exception.
claims.quote: Administrators can sign in to and manage Microsoft Intune without an assigned Intune license. This access is enabled by default for tenants created after July 2021 and applies to all administrator roles
claims.fix: Add to both the licensing notes and paragraph: 'Administrators can manage Intune without an assigned Intune licence when unlicensed admin access is enabled, which is the default for tenants created after July 2021. Older tenants can enable it; nested-group administrators still require an Intune licence.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/licensing#unlicensed-admin-access.

claims.claim: Microsoft Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > Create > Permissions reaches custom-role permissions.
claims.quote: choose Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > Create. ... On the Basics page, enter a name and description ... On the Permissions page, choose the permissions you want to use with this role.
claims.fix: Use the full route 'Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > Create > Basics > Permissions'. The omitted Basics page contains name and description fields, not a deciding policy or template choice.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/deviceManagement/roleDefinitions creates a role definition whose rolePermissions sets its allowed permissions.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/roleDefinitions ... rolePermissions ... List of Role Permissions this role is allowed to perform. These must match the actionName that is defined as part of the rolePermission.

claims.claim: Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > role > Assignments > + Assign is the route into the role assignment wizard.
claims.quote: go to Tenant administration > Roles > All roles. ... Select the role you want to assign and then select Assignments > + Assign. ... On the Admin Groups page, select Add groups ... On the Scope (Groups) page, add groups
claims.fix: Extend the route to 'Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > role > Assignments > + Assign > Basics > Admin Groups > Add groups > group > Scope (Groups)'. The printed route is correct but stops at the wizard entrance rather than its administrator and scope controls.

claims.claim: The cited POST /v1.0/deviceManagement/roleDefinitions/{roleDefinitionId}/roleAssignments reference documents setting both administrator groups and managed users or devices.
claims.quote: Searched: graph roleAssignment create Intune members resourceScopes deviceAndAppManagementRoleAssignment. Read generic and derived assignment create/resource references. The nested call documents resourceScopes, not members; derived create documents members at /roleAssignments.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api.call with 'POST /v1.0/deviceManagement/roleAssignments' and its docs with https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/intune-rbac-deviceandappmanagementroleassignment-create?view=graph-rest-1.0. Add to the note: 'Creates a deviceAndAppManagementRoleAssignment; the request body sets members for administrator security groups and resourceScopes for managed users or devices.' The existing generic roleAssignment reference documents resourceScopes but no members property.

claims.claim: The printed role-definition Graph call creates a new definition rather than editing an existing role's permissions.
claims.quote: Create a new roleDefinition object.

claims.claim: End users and devices are not affected by the permission split.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune granular endpoint security RBAC permissions existing custom roles migration automatic default Security baselines Antivirus Firewall Disk encryption. Read roadmap and manage-policies. They describe administrative permissions, but do not promise no effect on end users or devices.
claims.fix: Remove 'end users and devices are not affected by a permission split' from the impact rationale. Keep the low-impact judgement focused on administrators who author or hold roles.
